Mark the student's response to a question from Riverview Task 1 2022 (a Riverview Year 12 Business Studies assessment, Operations topic) strictly against the official marking criteria, exactly as an HSC marker would: award marks only for what is actually written, do not be generous, and quote the criteria row the response fits. Write feedback in short plain sentences and never comment on spelling or handwriting.

Question 13(a) [4 marks]: Explain TWO influences on operations that are currently having a negative impact on Aussie T Shirts.
STIMULUS / CASE INFORMATION:
Aussie T Shirts Pty Ltd is an Australian based manufacturer of clothing that has been producing these items from their Sydney factory for over 50 years. Recently they have lost several major long term supply contracts with large retailers. The feedback from these retailers was that their products were too expensive relative to other global suppliers.

MARKING CRITERIA (out of 4):
4 marks: Demonstrates a cause and effect relationship between TWO influences on operations and the negative impact on Aussie T Shirts
3 marks: Demonstrates a cause and effect relationship between ONE influence on operations and the negative impact on Aussie T Shirts and sketches in general terms the other influence and the negative impact
2 marks: Demonstrates a cause and effect relationship between ONE influence on operations and the negative impact OR sketches in general terms TWO influences and their negative impacts
1 marks: Sketches in general terms ONE influence on operations and the negative impact on operations


ANSWERS COULD INCLUDE (the student does not need every point):
Globalisation, cost-based competition, technology (or rather the lack of it), legal regulation (minimum wage, environmental regulations).

TEACHER MARKER COMMENTS:
Very well done overall. Many students detected and recalled appropriate syllabus influences from the stimulus. Some are still learning to address the NESA term explain to an appropriate depth of cause-and-effect argument; most of these gave a common-sense sketch that lacked the terminology and causation required for full marks.
